question: Which of the following is a tributary of Indus?
solution:
The correct answer is** Zaskar**

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points:__**

__
 
• ​__The Indus River originates at the confluence of the Sind river & the Gar river, which is Mansarovar Lake in Tibet. 
 
• This river takes a lengthy and tortuous course and passes through the Kashmir region. 
 
• It is the longest river in the subcontinent. 
 
• While it is about 3500 km long, 1500 km of it flows through Jammu and Kashmir. 
 
• The river banks are flanked by steep hills that have pine and deodar vegetation. 
 
• The Indus River flows in between the Ladakh range and the Zanskar range. 
 
• Indus has numerous tributaries, the principal among them are the Gilgit river, Gumal river, and Kabul river.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Son:

Son river originates from the Amarkantak plateau in the Anuppur district of Madhya Pradesh.

 
• It flows through Madhya Pradesh, Chhatisgarh, Uttar Pradesh, and Jharkhand and finally joins Ganga in Bihar near Patna.
 
• Ghaghra, Johilla, Chhoti Mahanadi, Gopad, Rihand, Kanhar, and North Koel are the tributaries of the Son river.
 
• The Bansagar Dam in Madhya Pradesh is also on the Son river.
 
• Indrapuri Dam has situated on the Son river in Dehri in the Rohtas district of Bihar.
 
 
• It is 1,407 meters (4,616 ft) long and the fourth-longest barrage in the world.
 
• The construction of the Indrapuri Dam was Started in the 1960s and was commissioned in 1968.
 
 

**Chambal:**

 
• Chambal originates from the Singar Chouri peak of Janapao Hills in the Mhow Indore district of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The Chambal River is a tributary of the Yamuna River in central India, and thus forms part of the greater Gangetic drainage system.
 
 
• In Rajasthan, it enters in Chittorgarh district near Chaurasigarh from Mandsor District in Madhya Pradesh.
 
 
 
• The river flows north-northeast through Madhya Pradesh, running for a time through Rajasthan, then forming the boundary between Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh before turning southeast to join the Yamuna in Uttar Pradesh.
